newsitem.title: USA: Pipe bombs discovered stored in Atlanta building.
newsitem.headline: Pipe bombs discovered stored in Atlanta building.

text.p: Federal investigators were examining four pipe bombs and a cache of bomb-making material discovered at a small roadside office building located just outside Atlanta, officials said on Tuesday.

The devices, some described by an eyewitness as being wrapped in shotgun shells, were handed over to the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms by local police to determine any possible link with last week's double-bombing at an abortion clinic located about 20 miles (32 km) away.
Investigators also were looking for similarities to the pipe bomb that exploded during the Summer Games last July in Atlanta's Centennial Olympic Park, leaving two dead and more than 100 injured.
Meanwhile, federal authorities said they were trying to contact a man said to have rented the room where the devices were discovered.
"There's nothing at this time to indicate that there's any link to the two bombings," ATF spokesman Bobby Browning said.

A local report said five bombs had been discovered in the Dekalb County community of Lithonia and described the site as a storage facility. Television footage pictured the building as a single-story woodframe structure.
"My understanding is that it's a small room in an office building," Browning said.
"There were four actual bombs and then items that could have been used to make more bombs," he added.
A janitor who was cleaning the room discovered the pipe bombs on Monday after knocking over a box.

An eyewitness told ABC-affiliate WSB-TV that the galvanised pipes were either three inches (eight cm) or six inches (15 cm) long and contained live fuses. The same eyewitness said some were wrapped in shotgun shells, apparently for "splatter effect."

"I can't comment on the construction or what exactly were in the devices. But they were actual live devices," Sgt. Rodney Rancifer, a Dekalb County bomb disposal technician, told the television station in an interview.

The officer added that he did not believe the pipe bombs were connected with last Thursday's explosions at the Atlanta Northside Family Planning Services centre in the city's Sandy Springs suburb. Six people were injured in those blasts.
